data.name: Mirsad
data.gender_notes: Mirsad is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A person who is a guide or a leader, someone who shows the way to others. The name Mirsad carries the meaning “Guide, Leader” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, English. Parents who choose Mirsad usually hope their child will grow to embody guide, leader and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A spiritual guide or leader, someone who helps others on their spiritual journey.
data.etymology: Mirsad belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Guide, Leader.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mirsad total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mirsad carries a strong cultural significance as it implies being a guiding figure and a leader. This name holds importance in Islamic culture where individuals who provide guidance and lead others to the right path are highly revered and respected. It is a name that embodies the essence of being a mentor, a teacher, or a spiritual guide.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Mirsad signifies being a beacon of light and a source of guidance for others. It is a name that imparts a deep sense of responsibility towards guiding and leading others towards the path of righteousness and spiritual growth. The name resonates with the idea of being a spiritual guide or a religious scholar, someone who has the knowledge and wisdom to help others navigate their spiritual journey. It is a name that symbolizes the noble and selfless act of teaching and leading others towards the truth and the light of God.

historical_references.reference: Mirsad al-Din Arabi, a Persian poet and scholar born in present-day Iran in 1213 CE. He wrote extensively on Sufism and Persian literature. Mirsad is considered one of the most influential figures in Persian literature.

Mirsad Ahmed Khan, a 19th-century Indian Muslim scholar and religious leader who founded the Farangi Mahal seminary in Saharanpur, India. The seminary was a center for Islamic learning and attracted scholars and students from all over South Asia. Mirsad is also known for his contributions to Urdu literature.
